scenario.name: Microsoft Threat Intel — Forest Blizzard (APT28): Print Spooler CVE-2022-38028 & GooseEgg
scenario.shortSubtitle: Microsoft Threat Intelligence · pnms009.inf Driver Store Symlink, GooseEgg (justice.exe) & wayzgoose.dll
scenario.overview: Imagine an ordinary office employee who wants master building keys without triggering front-door alarms. The employee edits a tiny text helper file tucked inside the official print-shop cabinet so the next time the building print foreman wakes up, the foreman automatically loads a rigged counterfeit print module with full building-master authority, unlocking a permanent secret back-office command room. In this scenario (CVE-2022-38028, Microsoft Threat Intel, Forest Blizzard (APT28): Print Spooler CVE-2022-38028 & GooseEgg) on WKS-GOV-03, the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: gooseEgg Modifies the Print Driver Registry, then forcing spoolsv.exe to Load the Rogue, then spawning a SYSTEM Command Shell. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering GooseEgg Modifies the Print Driver Registry, then Forcing spoolsv.exe to Load the Rogue, then Spawning a SYSTEM Command Shell, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: GOOSEEGG SYMLINK & PNMS009.INF DRIVERSTORE TAMPERING
stages.subtitle: justice.exe exploits CVE-2022-38028 to modify MPDW-constraints.js
stages.description: Running from a standard low-privilege user desk, the GooseEgg tool slips a crafted redirection into the print-driver registry shelf and alters a built-in JavaScript print-rule helper inside the system driver cabinet. On WKS-GOV-03.corp.local, starting from a standard low-privilege user session (which cannot install programs or read other users’ passwords), the attacker runs execute.bat which launches justice.exe (also referenced as doit.bat / justice.bat in some GooseEgg packages) to execute the GooseEgg binary. GooseEgg creates a custom printer driver key in the Registry and modifies mpdw-constraints.js (a JavaScript configuration file used by the built-in Microsoft XPS Document Writer printer driver to validate print ticket settings, crafted with oversized data to trigger CVE-2022-38028 when the Print Spooler reads it). When C:\Windows\System32\spoolsv.exe (which runs as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM) parses the malformed mpdw-constraints.js file inside the DriverStore\FileRepository directory, a memory corruption / permission flaw (CVE-2022-38028) allows the low-privilege user to overwrite the printer driver’s PnPData / DriverFile path. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ WRITE WAYZGOOSE.DLL / ⇠#1 ACK FileCreate) from Node ① (#1 GooseEgg Batch Launcher) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Microsoft Defender XDR).

stages.title: SPOOLSV.EXE LOADS WAYZGOOSE23.DLL AS SYSTEM
stages.subtitle: Print Spooler evaluates tampered JS constraint and loads malicious DLL
stages.description: When the Print Spooler foreman runs under supreme building authority to evaluate the altered print rules, it obediently loads the attacker unsigned counterfeit driver right into its own master-keyed memory room. With the driver path redirected by the exploit, GooseEgg drops its companion malicious library (wayzgoose.dll) into a writable folder and sends an RPC print-configuration call to wake up spoolsv.exe. Because spoolsv.exe runs as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM (the highest local operating-system account on Windows), when it calls LoadLibrary() on the registered printer driver, wayzgoose.dll is loaded directly into spoolsv.exe’s memory and executes with full SYSTEM master-key privileges. Instead of injecting memory into a SYSTEM process from the outside (which Windows Protected Process Light and EDR memory hooks block), CVE-2022-38028 tricks spoolsv.exe into voluntarily loading wayzgoose.dll as if it were an official Microsoft printer driver. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ SPOOLSV LOAD DLL / ⇠#2 ACK SYSTEM Load) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 DriverStore (pnms009.inf)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Microsoft Defender XDR).

stages.title: WHO.EXE SYSTEM BACKDOOR & COM SERVER HIJACK
stages.subtitle: Spawning SYSTEM command shell and registering ScheduledDefrag COM hijack
stages.description: Now holding master keys inside the print foreman's office, the rogue module launches an elevated command list to plant a durable secret side door and harvest badges across the compromised building. Now executing inside spoolsv.exe as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, wayzgoose.dll launches the attacker’s post-exploitation script (who.bat, which inherits spoolsv.exe’s SYSTEM security token so every command it runs has total control of the computer), registers a persistent Windows service backdoor, and opens an outbound C2 channel so Forest Blizzard can dump LSASS credentials and move laterally. In Windows, any child process created via CreateProcess inherits the security token of its parent process by default. However, because a legitimate Print Spooler (spoolsv.exe) should only talk to printers and never spawn cmd.exe or powershell.exe, this parent-child relationship is a classic high-confidence detection signal. In the documented Sysmon EID 1 exchange from DriverStore (pnms009.inf) to spoolsv.exe -> wayzgoose23.dll, spoolsv.exe -> wayzgoose23.dll responds with ACK PID 6240 (confirming that the SPAWN WHO.EXE request succeeded on spoolsv.exe -> wayzgoose23.dll and completing the final execution objective of Microsoft Threat Intel, Forest Blizzard (APT28): Print Spooler CVE-2022-38028 & GooseEgg). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ SPAWN WHO.EXE / ⇠#3 ACK PID 6240) from Node ③ (#3 DriverStore (pnms009.inf)) to Node ④ (#4 spoolsv.exe -> wayzgoose23.dll), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Microsoft Defender XDR).

detectionRule.title: Forest Blizzard GooseEgg File Creation in pnms009.inf DriverStore
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Forest Blizzard GooseEgg CVE-2022-38028 DriverStore Modification
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\DriverStore\FileRepository\pnms009.inf'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.dll'
      - '.js'
  filter_system:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\drvinst.exe'
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_system
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Apply the October 2022 Windows security update for CVE-2022-38028 and disable the Print Spooler service on servers that do not require printing.

detectionRule.title: Print Spooler (spoolsv.exe) Loading Unsigned DLL from DriverStore
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Spoolsv Loading Unsigned DLL (CVE-2022-38028 GooseEgg)
logsource:
  category: image_load
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\spoolsv.exe'
    ImageLoaded|contains: '\DriverStore\FileRepository\pnms009.inf'
    Signed: 'false'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Block unsigned DLL loads inside spoolsv.exe via Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules and audit DriverStore integrity.

detectionRule.title: Print Spooler Spawning Suspicious Child Process (GooseEgg who.exe)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Suspicious Child Process of Spoolsv.exe
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\spoolsv.exe'
    Image|contains:
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\Users\Public\'
      - '\Windows\Temp\'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Isolate any endpoint where spoolsv.exe spawns a child process from C:\ProgramData\ or C:\Windows\Temp\.
